narrative.overview:
Derived, not chosen: the direction contract's FORM is "Książeczka" (the passbook) and its OWN-WORLD block names off-white form paper, printed green ruling, typed entries, a handwritten heading and one violet stamp. Every line of the product is an entry and a balance stands after each one, and a page has both ends: a balance carried in on its first line and a balance carried forward on its last. The paper is form paper, not a dashboard: printed rules at a 2.5rem pitch carry the structure that a grid of cards would otherwise carry, the entries are typed in a typewriter face so that a column of money aligns on its decimal without help, and the headings and margin notes are written by hand, pinned to a printed rule rather than floating above the text. The book is kept by an adult; the hand is quick, not a schoolroom script, and the typewriter is a working tool, not a prop.

There is one stamp. Violet is the colour of a commanding action and of anything the product has settled: a primary button, a link, the current destination, the focus ring, the selected row, and the one "settled" mark itself - a typed word inside a one-pixel frame of stamp ink on the paper, beside the line that was carried in. It is never spent on what is planned: a page whose last entry is planned closes in pencil and is not stamped. A planned line is written in pencil - the second ink at `ink-2` - and the word "Planned" beside it is the channel; the grey only agrees. Nothing is ever struck through, because the product has no voided line. Green ink is money in hand, red ink is money overdrawn, brown ink is a warning, and each is text-grade at 7:1 on the darkest ground it can land on.

Nothing floats at rest. A slip laid on the paper has a one-pixel under-edge and nothing more, and the corners of everything are the corners a guillotine leaves (2-4px). Materials are at full strength: typed ink at 12.83:1, printed rules faint on purpose (1.44:1) so a page full of them reads as paper rather than as a grid. Dark is the same book read on a phone at night - slate paper, bone ink, lilac stamp - designed as a second set of values rather than inverted from the first. The three risks the world was built to avoid are: reading as school-like or childish (so the hand is bold, adult and never decorated), as retro or nostalgic (so there is no texture, no aged paper, no faux stamp graphic - the metaphor lives in rules and type only), and as too little like an application (so every control is a React Aria primitive with a 3:1 boundary, a 44px target and a two-ring focus indicator).
keyCharacteristics: Form paper (`canvas`), ruled in printed green at a 2.5rem pitch; the rules are the layout.
Two faces, two jobs: Caveat for anything written by hand, Courier Prime for anything read as a record - body, controls and every figure.
One violet stamp for every action and every "settled" mark; never on what is planned.
State is line form before hue: planned in pencil, booked in ink, nothing struck through.
Rules instead of cards; a heading over a body with a hairline above it is the unit of composition.
Square corners (2-4px); `full` radius only on things that are genuinely round.
Nothing floats at rest. The resting shadow is a one-pixel under-edge.
Every number that can change is set in the typewriter face and tabular.
Every colour token carries its measured contrast ratio beside its declaration.
Light and dark are two designed sets, both declared at three sites.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Violet is spent on what commands and on what is settled - the primary action, a link, the current destination, the focus ring, the selected row. It is never spent on a planned line, a decoration, a heading or a divider. "Settled" has its own mark now - the `settled` badge tone, a typed word in a one-pixel `brand` frame on the paper, not on a wash - and it is the only status that may carry `brand`. If a screen needs a second violet thing, one of them is not an action.

rules.name: The Pencil Rule
rules.body: A planned entry is written in `ink-2` with the word beside it; a booked entry is written in `ink`. State is line form before hue, and nothing is ever struck through.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Third Rule
rules.body: Money direction is never encoded by colour alone, and colour is not even the first channel: every amount carries an explicit sign, inflow is set at the bold weight and outflow at regular, a transfer carries a repeat glyph, and the product stays correct with all colour removed. The measured dichromat separation of the green and red inks is the reason.

rules.name: The Measured Pair Rule
rules.body: Every colour token that can meet text carries its measured contrast ratio as a trailing comment beside its declaration in `tokens.css`, and the contrast test recomputes every one on each run. A token added without its measurement is not finished.

rules.name: The Three-Site Rule
rules.body: Every themed colour is declared in exactly three places: bare `:root`, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, and `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. Fewer than three produces a toggle that works in one direction only.

rules.name: The Typed Line Rule
rules.body: A line of the passbook is a 2.5rem box - one rule of the form - and its baseline sits 3px above the printed rule, placed by a translate (`translate-y-[calc(1rem-0.22em)]` for the typewriter at label size) so paint moves and layout does not. A cell has no vertical padding, and the rule under it is drawn as an inset one-pixel shadow rather than a border so it adds no height and the table never walks off the pitch.

rules.name: The Hand-On-Rules Rule
rules.body: A handwritten heading on ruled paper is placed on the rules the same way: the hero by `translate-y-[calc(2.5rem-0.33em)]`, a title by `leading-10` plus `translate-y-[calc(1.25rem-0.33em)]`. A hand that floats between rules reads as a sticker.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Anything read as a record is typed; anything said by the keeper is written. A heading, a margin note or a section title is Caveat; a figure, a label, a button, a cell or a paragraph is Courier Prime. A figure is never set in the hand and a heading is never typed.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change carries `.tabular` on the element holding the digits. The face is monospaced already; the utility stays so a re-rendered total still asks for tabular figures should the face ever change under it.

rules.name: The Real Minus Rule
rules.body: A negative amount is prefixed with U+2212, not a hyphen, and a positive inflow carries an explicit `+`. Zero is written unsigned.

rules.name: The Spoken-Sentence Rule
rules.body: A money cell carries two strings: the drawing, `aria-hidden`, and a full sentence in an `sr-only` span that names the currency in full and the direction in words.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: A section, a list item or a callout is a heading over a body with a hairline above it. A card is a slip laid on the paper for content that genuinely needs its own ground (a chart, a form); it is never the scaffold of a page.

rules.name: The On-Pitch Rule
rules.body: Anything drawn on ruled paper is a whole number of rules tall. A line box is a length (2.5rem), not a ratio, and a cell adds no padding the rule did not budget for.

rules.name: The Closed-Ladder Rule
rules.body: Nothing invents a `z-index`. Eight named rungs (`base` 0, `nav` 30, `dropdown` 40, `overlay` 50, `modal` 60, `popover` 65, `tooltip` 70, `toast` 80).

rules.name: The Focus Reserve Rule
rules.body: Nothing clips a focus ring; a scroll container that could crop one reserves `--focus-reserve` (4px) of padding.

rules.name: The Under-Edge Rule
rules.body: A resting surface gets a tone and a one-pixel under-edge, never a blur. If a card needs a shadow to read as a card, its ground or its rule is wrong.

rules.name: The One-Pixel Press Rule
rules.body: A press is `translate-y-px` and one shadow step down - never a bounce, never a scale. The control reads as pushed into the paper.

rules.name: The Tone-In-Dark Rule
rules.body: In dark the grounds separate further and the shadows are re-declared opaque; a dark value computed from a light one is a defect.

rules.name: The Guillotine Rule
rules.body: No radius above 4px on a rectangle. A rounded rectangle is a pill and a pill is a sticker; the form has neither.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Stripe Rule
rules.body: No coloured border wider than 1px on a card, a list item, a callout or an alert; the spine before the balance column (2px `border-panel`) is the one heavier rule and it is neutral. A selected or current thing is framed by a one-pixel line, never striped by a bar.

rules.name: The Boundary Honesty Rule
rules.body: If a box can be clicked or typed into, its border is `border-strong`. If it cannot, its border is `border-subtle` or `border-panel`. A decorative `border-strong` is a defect.

rules.name: The Pending-Not-Disabled Rule
rules.body: A submit in flight uses `isPending`: focusable, `aria-disabled`, label kept in the DOM under the spinner so the button holds its width.

dos: **Do** set every heading, margin note and section title in Caveat, and every figure, label, control and paragraph in Courier Prime.
**Do** put a line of the passbook in a 2.5rem box with its baseline 3px above the rule by a translate, and draw the rule under a cell as an inset one-pixel shadow.
**Do** build a section, a list or a summary as headings over bodies on `border-t` rules; reach for a card only when the content needs its own ground.
**Do** spend violet on actions and on what is settled - the primary button, links, the current destination, the focus ring, the selected row - and nowhere else.
**Do** write a planned line in `ink-2` with the word beside it, and a booked line in `ink`.

**Do** mark what is settled with the `settled` badge - a typed word in a one-pixel `brand` frame on the paper - and give a page both ends: a balance carried in on the first line and a balance carried forward, read not retyped, on the last, over the heavier `border-panel` rule.
**Do** give every amount an explicit sign (U+2212 for out, `+` for in), set inflow bold and outflow regular, and mark a transfer with the repeat glyph.
**Do** mark a current or selected thing with a one-pixel frame or a one-pixel rule in `brand`.
**Do** keep every radius at 2-4px on a rectangle and reserve `full` for things that are round.
**Do** record every colour token's measured contrast beside its declaration and declare every themed colour at all three sites.
**Do** grow hit areas to 44px inside the primitive with `target-min`, write `outline-solid` explicitly, and keep a pending button's label in the DOM.
**Do** use lucide icons only, and use the same glyph for the same meaning everywhere.

**Do** hold WCAG 2.2 AA as the CI gate (axe on every route) and the named AAA criteria the product claims: 2.5.5 target size, 2.4.11 and 2.4.12 focus not obscured, 1.4.8 visual presentation, 2.2.6 timeouts, 3.3.9 accessible authentication, and the 7:1 text floor.
donts: **Don't** place an eyebrow, kicker or uppercase label above a heading. Micro uppercase is for a column heading or a `dt` on the same line as its figure, never a line above a title.
**Don't** use cards as the scaffold of a page, or a grid of equal icon cards as a section.
**Don't** build a hero-metric tile - a big number over a small label. A figure is a typed line with its label at the start and the figure at the end.
**Don't** set a figure in the hand or a heading in the typewriter.
**Don't** use gradient text, glass, blur, a translucent bar, or a hard offset shadow anywhere.
**Don't** put a coloured border wider than 1px on a card, list item, callout or alert, or mark selection with a bar; the 2px spine is neutral and belongs to the balance column only.
**Don't** put a radius above 4px on a rectangle; no pills on chips, badges or panels.
**Don't** use emoji, a glyph icon set, or a system display face; icons are lucide and the faces are the two self-hosted ones.

**Don't** spend violet on a planned line, a decoration, a heading or a divider; never put the `settled` mark on a planned line or stamp a page that closes in pencil; and don't strike anything through - there is no voided line.
**Don't** add texture, aged paper, a faux stamp graphic, or a decorative flourish; the metaphor lives in rules and type, and the world must not read as retro or as a schoolbook.
**Don't** paint text in a series colour, encode direction or status by colour alone, abbreviate money outside a chart axis, or render an amount from a float.
**Don't** use negative tracking on either face.
**Don't** invent a `z-index`, hard-code a dimension off the 4px grid, animate a layout property, or ship an animation without the reduced-motion path.
**Don't** fabricate evidence on any surface: no users, testimonials, ratings, prices, uptime or security claims, no bank-sourced implication, and never the reference product's name.
**Don't** claim blanket WCAG AAA conformance; `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md` states exactly what is claimed and this document never contradicts it.
**Don't** add a dependency to express any of the above; the stack is frozen (`docs/SPEC.md` §3).
